messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
Memory: one remembered fact per line, with the dates it held and the note that recorded it. An indented "earlier" line is a version of the fact above it that was later corrected.
- [decision] Reindex jobs will page on failure. (since 2025-10-07; source incident-review/INC-2025-023)
- The root cause of INC-2025-023 was a reindex job that failed silently on a full disk. (since 2025-10-07; source incident-review/INC-2025-023)
- [constraint] The indexer is pinned to OpenSearch 2.11, and the pin lifts when the full reindex completes. (since 2025-04-22; source standup/cinder/2025-04-22)
- [decision] As of 2025-12-18, the indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write, since incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes. (since 2025-12-18; source standup/atlas/2025-12-18)
- INC-2025-023 was an indexer incident on 2025-10-03 in which the indexer served stale results for two days. (since 2025-10-07; source incident-review/INC-2025-023)
- The root cause of INC-2025-011 was an index missing after the schema migration. (since 2025-05-30; source incident-review/INC-2025-011)
- The job scheduler's single fixed node turned every restart into a missed run. (since 2025-06-06; source standup/ember/2025-06-06)
- The Boreal team noticed that the indexer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the indexer's owners. (since 2026-02-10; source standup/boreal/2026-02-10-2)
- INC-2026-009 was an incident in which the job scheduler ran the nightly jobs twice on 2026-05-16. (since 2026-05-19; source incident-review/INC-2026-009)
- The Atlas team noticed that the indexer's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners. (since 2026-05-27; source standup/atlas/2026-05-27)
- As of 2025-09-23, the pager for the job scheduler rings the Cinder team. (since 2025-09-23; source handover/2025-09-23-scheduler)
- As of 2026-04-01, the pager for the indexer rings the Boreal team, not the Atlas team. (since 2026-04-01; source handover/2026-04-01-search-indexer)
- Team Dune observed that the indexer's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change. (since 2026-06-09; source standup/dune/2026-06-09)
- As of 2026-05-22, the job scheduler's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump, per a heads-up from team Dune. (since 2026-05-22; source standup/dune/2026-05-22-3)
- The indexer depends on the product catalog for product documents. (since 2025-01-30; source standup/cinder/2025-01-30)
- The Atlas team noticed that the image resizer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the image resizer's owners. (since 2025-10-15; source standup/atlas/2025-10-15)
- The job scheduler is not the Boreal team's service, so the Boreal team flagged it. (since 2025-12-01; source standup/boreal/2025-12-01-2)
- [constraint] As of 2025-08-19, deploys to the job scheduler happen only on Tuesdays and Fridays between 09:00 and 10:30 UTC; the old Tuesday 13:00-15:00 UTC window is retired. (since 2025-08-19; source standup/dune/2025-08-19)
  - earlier: [constraint] Deploys to the job scheduler happen only on Tuesdays between 13:00 and 15:00 UTC. (held 2025-02-06 to 2025-08-19; source standup/ember/2025-02-06)
- The root cause of INC-2026-003 was a retry loop that ignored idempotency keys. (since 2026-02-26; source incident-review/INC-2026-003)
- The Atlas team observed that the reports pipeline's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change. (since 2025-12-25; source standup/atlas/2025-12-25)
